description: Somos un equipo multidisciplinario apasionado por la ciencia, la tecnología y la innovación. Reunimos conocimientos en desarrollo de software, inteligencia artificial, electrónica y análisis de datos para afrontar desafíos relacionados con la exploración espacial.
summary:
We developed software to track astronauts' cardiovascular and behavioral health before, during, and after long-duration missions in microgravity. It gathers measurements from authorized equipment and crew logs to identify changes from their baseline and highlight findings requiring medical review. The report describes the proposal, development plan, and prototype evaluation on Earth. We approached this challenge based on two factors astronauts may face: cardiovascular events and mental health issues. Using the astronaut's own data, our predictive software estimates the risk of cardiovascular events or behavioral problems.

During flight, blood pressure can drop even if cardiac output increases. To interpret measurements, it's important to know the mission phase, previous activity, and method used. Repeated measurements under comparable conditions help identify trends. Follow-up distinguishes adaptation during flight from the response to gravity after landing (Norsk et al., 2015).

Sleep loss, irregular schedules, and confinement can affect attention, performance, and emotional well-being. The cognitive battery measures performance, while questionnaires and self-reports help understand symptoms and their daily impact. Clinical assessment considers the circumstances, consistency of changes, and crew member reports during interviews (Hardy et al., 2025; NASA, n.d.-a).
details: Our project is a monitoring system that through a mobile app developed in Flutter with a Python backend, sends voice and video in real time, and at the same time receives alerts in case something goes wrong with your health. It also has a chatbot, which is intended to be an advisor on medical and psychological issues. We have a desktop application that processes the data collected by sensors or wearable devices, giving a broader view of the collected data and the predictions generated. This app is entirely developed in Python. And as the last app of our project, we have a specific version for doctors on Earth. This app will receive a report with the collected data and the predictions made, and like the previous one, it is developed in Python. We aim to make an impact on the problem by preventing it. The goal of our project is to detect warning signs before it's too late, preventing them. that cause long-term damage to both physical and psychological health. We focused on making interfaces extremely understandable for anyone, and we also looked at data collection from another perspective. We were interested in collecting data through voice and video, converting it into vectors to later generate a report for the psychologist assigned to that astronaut. The data we considered include cardiovascular health data like blood pressure or cardiac output, and behavioral factors, such as changes in voice tone or the astronaut's expressions.
